subject: Transient throughput sponsorship and de-escalation path
messages:
From: Alyssa Grant <alyssa@clearwave.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@clearwave.com
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Launch week uplift — sponsorship idea and liability question

Hi Priyom,

We’re gearing up for a big feature toggle on May 3 — expectation is a 4x spike in generation volume for ~72 hours. From our side we can commit to a 6-month paid plan after launch if we get a short runway to succeed.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood provide a temporary throughput uplift for launch day (90th-99th percentile QPS buffer) without us immediately upgrading the commit?
- If we do exceed committed quota, would Redwood consider a partial sponsorship/credit for the overrun for this specific launch window in exchange for a 6-month commitment we sign within 30 days?

I’m attaching last month’s usage slice to show the pattern. Also want to understand how billing/true-up would look (overnight invoice vs monthly reconciliation). Can you point me to the path?

Thanks — Alyssa
Alyssa Grant
Head of Platform, ClearWave
[attachment: ClearWave_usage_Mar2027.csv]

---
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Grant <alyssa@clearwave.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Launch week uplift — sponsorship idea and liability question

Hi Alyssa — thanks, and congrats on the upcoming toggle.

Quick notes: we can absolutely support a short-lived uplift. To make the path low-friction for both sides I want to align internally on three things before we confirm:
1) Capacity envelope (QPS headroom target) — can you confirm an expected peak and duration?
2) Desired billing treatment — do you prefer a one-off uplift invoice or to handle as a monthly true-up?
3) Any legal/contract guardrails you need around automatic throttles or hard caps.

Ben (cc’d), can you draft a provisional pricing sketch once Alyssa confirms the numbers?

I’ll loop Finance if we agree to a sponsored credit so they can outline the accounting/credit flow.

Best,
Priyom
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

---
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Grant <alyssa@clearwave.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed uplift structure for ClearWave (provisional)

Hi Alyssa — based on the usage file, quick provisional that we can fine-tune:

Proposal (short window, provisional):
- Temporary uplift window: May 3 00:00 UTC — May 5 23:59 UTC (72 hours).
- Provisioned headroom: +350% baseline QPS (we'll size exact GPU concurrency after you confirm target).
- Billing/true-up: we can do a one-time invoice for the uplift at a blended overrun rate (midpoint between PAYG and committed tier) OR include the uplift as a monthly true-up line on May invoice.
- Sponsored credit: Redwood offers a one-time promotional credit equal to 40% of the uplift invoice if ClearWave signs a 6-month commit at the proposed committed rate within 30 days of launch. Credit applies to the following invoice, not retroactively to the uplift itself.
- Cap option: we can offer a per-minute hard cap that prevents costs beyond X (you set X) — this is normally our conservative default, but it can increase risk of throttling.

Attachments: draft SOW to capture the path and responsibilities.
[attachment: SOW_v1_ClearWave.pdf]

If you want, Connor can coordinate the technical plan for KV cache warm-up and prefix caching to reduce billable tokens during the surge.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager — Redwood Inference

---
From: Alyssa Grant <alyssa@clearwave.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 08:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed uplift structure for ClearWave (provisional)

Thanks Ben — appreciate the clear proposal. A few clarifying redlines from Legal/ProdOps:
1) Credit timing: the proposed credit applying to the following invoice is acceptable, but we need it to be guaranteed in the SOW with a fallback to invoice credit if the signed commit is delayed up to 45 days (we can accept 45 days).
2) Cap: we prefer a soft cap (alerts at threshold + throttling only if we hit a higher emergency cap) rather than a hard minute-by-minute cutoff. Production team prefers predictability over sudden failures.
3) Liability: we need a clause that ensures Redwood will make reasonable efforts to avoid throttling during the uplift window; emergency throttles must be preceded by 10 minute notice via our Ops channel.

I attached our suggested contract redlines. Also want a short note on how the blended overrun rate is calculated so procurement can model it.
[attachment: redlines_contract_20270408.docx]

—Alyssa

---
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Alyssa Grant <alyssa@clearwave.com>
Date: Fri, 8 Apr 2027 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed uplift structure for ClearWave (provisional) — finance notes

Hi all — looping Finance in. A few operational notes that will affect how we book the credit: 

- If we issue a promotional credit tied to a signed commit we need an explicit acceptance matrix (SOW signature + PO number) to avoid revenue recognition complications. Please capture that in the SOW (I can supply a clause).
- For the blended overrun rate: we calculate as (0.5 * PAYG_rate + 0.5 * committed_unit_rate) by default; we can adjust split if Sales/Customer prefer different economics but document must state the formula.
- If ClearWave requires a soft cap + notice workflow, we’ll need to run a short Ops playbook (15–30 min) with their SREs pre-launch and capture sign-off.

I can approve the 40% promotional credit contingent on an internal finance ticket and the acceptance matrix being in the SOW.

Laura Bennett
Head of Billing Operations — Redwood Inference

---
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Grant <alyssa@clearwave.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 9 Apr 2027 10:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Launch week uplift — sponsorship idea and liability question — agreed path

Alyssa/Team — thanks for the quick turn. Summary of the agreed provisional path and next steps: 

1) Uplift window: May 3 00:00 UTC — May 5 23:59 UTC (72 hours) with provisioned headroom at +350% baseline. Connor will send the technical plan and warm-up checklist by Apr 12.
2) Billing: uplift will appear as a one-time uplift invoice; customer may elect monthly true-up instead — confirm which you prefer by Apr 15.
3) Sponsored credit: 40% of the uplift invoice credited to your next invoice if ClearWave signs the 6-month committed plan within 45 days of launch AND provides a PO number referenced in the SOW. Laura will attach Finance clause.
4) Cap & notices: Redwood to implement soft cap alerts at threshold and emergency cap throttling only after a 10-minute Ops notification. We will run a 20-minute ops playbook with ClearWave SREs prior to May 3.
5) Legal: Ben to incorporate Alyssa’s redlines and Laura’s acceptance matrix into SOW v1. Ben, please send updated SOW by Apr 12 for signature routing.

Action items:
- Connor O'Brien: deliver technical warm-up plan (by 2027-04-12).
- Ben Carter: update SOW + pricing line item with blended rate formula and credit clause (by 2027-04-12).
- Alyssa/ClearWave: confirm billing preference (one-time uplift invoice vs monthly true-up) by 2027-04-15 and provide PO when signed.
- Laura Bennett: create internal finance ticket and copy the acceptance matrix clause into the SOW.

If anyone sees anything missing, flag it here and we’ll adjust. Otherwise I’ll prepare the HubSpot deal update and mark the uplift milestone.

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
